entities.summary:
Clearchus of Rhegium (b. 550 BCE) was a renowned Greek musician and composer of the Classical era, active in the city of Rhegium in southern Italy. His contributions to the development of music in the ancient Greek world were significant, as he helped to shape the sound of Greek tragedy and comedy.

As a painter and sculptor, Clearchus was also a prominent figure in the artistic circles of ancient Greece, collaborating with other notable artists of the time. His work had a lasting impact on the evolution of Greek art, influencing generations of artists to come.

Despite the passage of time, Clearchus of Rhegium's legacy continues to be felt in the modern world, with his compositions and artistic style remaining an important part of Greek cultural heritage. His influence can be seen in various forms of Western classical music and art, a testament to the enduring power of his creative vision.

The most striking statistic about Clearchus of Rhegium is that he was a contemporary of the famous Greek historian Herodotus, with whom he likely collaborated on various artistic and literary projects.
